title: Wterm 0.5.0: измеренная отзывчивость и воспроизводимый dev-контур
description:
Контекст: BB-плагин wterm-terminal-preview, repo /home/ubuntu/Projects/bb-wterm-terminal-plugin. Цель — отзывчивый ввод и клики без потери PTY-данных и существующих функций. На старом несогласованном стенде click→DOM rows: 873 мс, с profiler 1261 мс; openWterm начал запрос через754 мс, сам запрос28 мс, max main task396 мс. Это два loopback-наблюдения, НЕ p95 и НЕ input-to-paint. Установленные 0.4.0 не соответствовали lock0.5.0; с 2026-09-06 пакеты core/dom/react/ghostty реально0.5.0, npm ls чистый,120 тестов прошли. Старые package-internal выводы нужно перепроверять на0.5.0. Запрещено обещать ускорение без before/after. Изменение семантики владения PTY или API требует согласования пользователя. Не отключать глобальные плагины и не трогать чужие терминалы. Unit + browser checks обязательны для затронутого поведения. Не удалять файлы и не коммитить/пушить без разрешения. Перед работой br show/claim; зависимости — blockers, не просто ссылки. Общие файлы менять последовательно с reservation/координацией.

# Synthetic missing sessions are unavailable, not running

## Background
ISA ISC-26, ISC-27. ANALYSIS §9.2 step 3.

`unavailableLinkedSession` currently sets `status: "running"` and `updatedAt: 0`. Picker shows Running · 01.01.1970. `evaluateTerminalPresence` treats running as `ready`, so the panel opens a WebSocket to a missing PTY and `scheduleReconnect` loops forever with no error.

Intent of `running` was “don’t kill the tab on a blip.” TTL bead covers blips. Lying about health is worse.

## Background
ISA ISC-31, must preserve ISC-8. ANALYSIS PERF-04.

## Background
ISA F7 ISC-39, ISC-40, ISC-41, ISC-42, ISC-43. Principal 2026-09-04: a new terminal / new tab must open a new session, not the previous one.

README already claims every Wterm tab starts an independent session. `threadPanelAction.run` does `createTerminal` then `openPanel({ params: { terminalId } })`. Other paths steal last PTY:

1. **`LegacyTerminalAction`**: `currentParams = hasTerminalParams(params) ? params : fallbackParams` from **thread-scoped** localStorage. A new tab with empty host params **is** the previous terminal.
2. **Composer `OpenSessionTerminalAction`**: passes `readLastTerminalId` into `revealSessionTerminalPanel`. Fine only if it reveals an already-open panel. A newly created panel must not steal last id.
3. **`resolveSessionTerminalId`** hardcodes `openTabCount: 0`, so `reusableTerminalId` always considers reuse even when tabs are mounted/pending. `wtermOpenCount` already exists (mounted + pending).
4. Planned picker “Reopen last” (ISC-30) is dropped.

Same-tab remount without host params: empty params must show Picker, not last id. Losing remount convenience is better than every new tab being last PTY. Do not invent a second thread-scoped fallback.

## Technical approach
- Keep `run()` always `createTerminal` + params = new id.
- Extract `initialPanelParams(hostParams): host | null` — never reads localStorage. `LegacyTerminalAction` uses that. Still **write** last id when a real session is shown.
- `resolveSessionTerminalId` takes `openTabCount` (default from `wtermOpenCount(threadId)` at call site). Composer reveal: if a Wterm tab is already open, reveal it; if this gesture opens a new panel/tab, `createTerminal`.
- Tests: last id in storage + empty host params → not that id; `openTabCount > 0` → no reuse; existing `reusableTerminalId` tests stay.
- Coordinate `app.tsx` with picker bead (`wterm-speed-feel-ftz.6`): this bead owns last-id/open policy; picker owns loading/failed UI. Prefer implementing this after picker in the same file (depends on .6) to reduce merge fights, or one agent both.

## Success criteria
- New tab + stored last id + empty params does not mount last session
- `run()` always creates
- Picker New terminal creates
- Composer does not bind a new tab to last id when openTabCount > 0
- Two sequential new tabs → two distinct ids (headed ISC-42)

- `npm test`

HostTerminalAction already uses host params only — do not add localStorage there. Do not delete `readLastTerminalId`; still written after create/select. P0.

description:
# Read path for linked terminals must not take the write mutex

## Background
ISA ISC-24. ANALYSIS §9.2 (critical multi-tab stall).

`withLinkedTerminalIds` serializes per-thread KV updates. `loadLinkedTerminals` incorrectly runs **inside** that mutex and awaits `Promise.allSettled(linkedIds.map(terminals.get))` — N host round-trips while holding the exclusive lock. Callers: `listSessions` (verify loop every 400ms, picker), `sessionsForThread` (upload), create/remember, restart. Two tabs → O(tabs × N × RTT) stalls. This also explains BUG-03: verify’s listSessions queues behind the same create’s remember.

## Technical approach
1. `linkedTerminalIds(bb, threadId)` snapshot **without** write lock.
2. Fan-out `terminals.get` **outside** the lock.
3. Return sessions + unavailable ids immediately for RPC.
4. If host returns a replacement id, `void withLinkedTerminalIds` later: re-read `current`, remap only ids still present, `saveLinkedTerminalIds`. Catch and ignore (best-effort).
5. `withLinkedTerminalIds` remains for `rememberLinkedTerminal` and restart rewrites only.

Upload path must use sessions that actually exist; do not authorize upload to unavailable ids.

Concurrency test: delay `terminals.get`; start listSessions; then createTerminal/remember; remember must complete without waiting for the delayed gets.

## Success criteria
- listSessions does not await other listSessions’ host GETs via the write gate
- create remember is not blocked by in-flight list fan-out
- replacement id reconcile does not drop a concurrently remembered new id

## Test plan
- `server.test.ts` fake sdk with controllable delay
- Existing thread-scope upload/restart tests still pass
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Implement after or with KV record parser if signatures change. Do not “fix” by increasing verify retries only. Hot file `server.ts` — one agent with nerd-font-cache and unavailable/TTL if possible.

# Linked-ID KV expand–contract with dead-ID TTL

## Background
ISA ISC-25. ANALYSIS §9.2 step 2.

`nextLinkedTerminalIds` keeps an id forever when `terminals.get` rejects. N grows for the life of the thread; every listSessions pays N timeouts inside (today) the mutex. Need a bounded list without treating a 1s host blip as death.

## Technical approach
Type:
```
interface LinkedTerminalRecord {
  id: string;
  firstUnavailableAt: number | null;
}
const DEAD_TERMINAL_GRACE_MS = 60_000;
```

`parseLinkedRecords(unknown)`:
- array of strings → `{id, firstUnavailableAt: null}` (legacy)
- array of objects with string `id` → use numeric `firstUnavailableAt` or null
- anything else skipped

On get fulfilled: stamp null (live).
On get rejected: set stamp to now if null; if `now - stamp > 60s`, drop id.
Writes may persist records. Reads must still accept legacy `string[]` forever.

Time: inject a `now: () => number` in the pure function for tests.

Do not require a one-shot migration job.

## Success criteria
- Legacy KV arrays still load
- Live success clears stamp
- Rejected id survives <60s
- Rejected id drops after 60s
- N cannot grow unbounded from permanent failures

## Test plan
- Pure parser + next-state tests (preferred new `linked-terminal-records.ts` so server stays thin)
- `server.test.ts` round-trip if KV mock exists
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Split into `linked-terminal-records.ts` to avoid merge hell with read-path and font cache. Server imports the parser. Clock freeze in tests.
